finding: The site has no live range for this job, so there is nothing to grade; this file is a first build, revised on a second pass. Built totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks; oil = the maker's capacity with filter in quarts x a per-quart price, plus one filter): economy Toyota Corolla 1.8L (4.4 qt) about $63-$168; midsize 2016 Toyota Camry 2.5L (4.6 qt) about $64-$170; truck Chevrolet Silverado 1500 5.3L (8.0 qt) about $87-$225; luxury Lexus ES 350 3.5L (6.4 qt) about $77-$188. Against the benchmarks: a chain price survey found full synthetic at $45 (Walmart) to $100 (Valvoline, Firestone Premium), $65 at a local mechanic and $109 at a dealer; a second article puts Walmart's full synthetic at about $59-$65; a third gives $65-$125 for full synthetic; RepairPal's national average of $160-$188 is a high outlier. So the low end of the build ($63-$87) lands in the middle of real menu prices, while the high end ($168-$225) is above most of what the benchmarks show for an ordinary car and close to RepairPal. That gap is expected: an oil change is sold at a menu price rather than built up from parts and hourly labor, and a build that charges list-price genuine oil plus up to 45 minutes at $160/hr overstates what most drivers pay. The menu-price benchmarks ($45-$125 for a full synthetic service that typically includes up to five quarts) are the better guide to a real bill, with extra quarts charged on top for the truck and the V6. What changed on this pass: every oil capacity now comes from the maker's owner's manual, and every high figure is an OEM list price per quart multiplied by that capacity plus the filter at list. To get there the examples were changed: the economy car is the 2010 Corolla (its manual loaded; the 2015 car uses the same 1.8L engine and the same 4.4-quart figure per a non-maker data sheet), the truck is a Silverado 1500 with GM's own list prices in place of a Ford kit price, and the luxury car is a Lexus ES 350 in place of the BMW, whose manual and genuine oil list price could not be loaded. Caveats, stated plainly: the Corolla and Lexus manual pages were read on manuals-hosting sites, not the makers' own sites; the Camry manual is on Toyota Canada's site but the pages read do not print the model name or year (it is identified by its two engines); the Silverado manual read is the later Silverado LD edition (copyright 2018) of the same truck and engine, and the page naming its oil viscosity was not read, so 0W-20 is to be confirmed; the Lexus oil price is the Toyota catalog's list price for Toyota Genuine oil. How solid the hours are: they are general, not vehicle-specific, and none is a maker's time. The low end is a quick-lube chain's own '15 minutes or less' and the high end is two independent repair shops' '30 to 45 minutes'. No maker document with a separate time for an oil and filter change was found; the nearest is a Honda bulletin that allows 0.6 hr for an oil replacement bundled with software updates, which fits inside the range. Posted menu prices, added 2026-11-20: eight sellers' own pages (three chains, two independent shops and three dealers, in VA, NC, PA, CA, NJ and AZ plus two nationwide chains) post a full synthetic oil and filter change at $59.95 to $109, most of them between about $73 and $90 and usually for up to five quarts, with tax, shop fees and extra quarts on top; several do not name the viscosity and three of the prices are coupons or specials.
extras: A quote often adds a charge per extra quart beyond the five a menu price usually includes (one survey reports $5-$10 a quart at one chain), which matters for the truck (8.0 quarts) and the V6 (6.4), plus shop supplies and an oil disposal or environmental fee, a new drain plug washer, and sales tax. Many menu prices bundle a tire rotation, fluid top-offs and a multi-point inspection. Engine and cabin air filters, wiper blades and other fluid services are commonly offered at the same visit and priced separately. Cartridge-style filters and under-engine covers can add a little time.
